queries.prompt: Analyze what traffic is going through our AWS NAT Gateway from flow logs in GB and % and check why S3 traffic is still hitting NAT despite a Gateway Endpoint.
Why is our NAT Gateway volume so high, which VPC Flow Logs (`interface-id`) should we query for NAT analysis, and is a Cross-Region S3 Interface Endpoint safe to recommend?
Trace which AWS service or customer-owned resource sits behind the top destination IPs in our NAT Gateway VPC Flow Logs.

Our EKS worker nodes in private subnets already have `ecr.api` and `ecr.dkr` Interface Endpoints, yet `BytesOutToDestination` on `nat-0abc123` spikes by hundreds of gigabytes every time pods pull container images!
Why are our private microservices sending 2 TB a week through `nat-09988` to our own Elastic IP `13.127.88.40` when active VPC Peering already connects the two VPCs?
Before we enable Private DNS on a Cross-Region S3 Interface Endpoint to stop cross-region S3 reads from traversing NAT, what S3 API operation could silently break across our entire VPC?
Flow logs on `eni-0nat555` over 14 days show `4,500 GB` to `52.219.64.0/22` (`ap-south-1` S3), `3,000 GB` to `52.216.0.0/15` (`us-east-1` S3), and `1,500 GB` to `AMAZON` IPs. Categorize and diagnose.
A teammate pulled flow logs from EC2 instance `eni-0inst111` instead of `nat-0111`'s ENI to measure how many GB crossed NAT—explain why those numbers are wrong and how to query the right ENI.
CloudTrail filtered on `sourceIPAddress = 13.232.100.50` (our NAT EIP) shows 2.4M calls to `logs.amazonaws.com` and `sts.amazonaws.com`—check our Interface Endpoint coverage.
VPC Flow Logs on `eni-0db111` show `ACCEPT` on TCP SYN to port `5432` and `REJECT` on the outbound `SYN-ACK`—determine whether an SG or NACL dropped it.
Simulate whether adding a Route 53 Resolver `FORWARD` rule for `.corp` will shadow our `internal.corp` Private Hosted Zone inside `vpc-0167f5c4bb94b89db`.
Explain why AS-path prepending on a Mumbai Direct Connect VIF does not override Direct Connect Gateway local-region preference.
